content.description: WAVE 2 BUILD (Lane 2). HIGH-FLIP-RISK: the public-read-vs-read tier boundary -- independent second reviewer owed. Wave-1 #11695 ALREADY landed the Next guard, its token-guard.test.mjs, and CI wiring -- do NOT rebuild them; re-derive from origin/main (the wave-1 ledger self-staled). Recipe: tooling/grip/ledger/w2-capabilities-additive-safety-2026-08-17.md. DEFECT: @read_perms ~w(read admin public-read) (tenancy/auth.ex:46) collapses three permissions to auth_tier "read", so both build guards (`tier === 'read'`) accept a plain read/admin token and bake it into a browser bundle. PART A -- API attestation (the ONLY additive-safe shape is Option A). Add an OPT-IN root key ?perms=1 -> "permissions": [<caller's verbatim permission list>] ([] for anon, emitted even for anon so absent!=empty is unambiguous). NOT an unconditional key (released bp strict-decodes the root via manifest.go:168 DisallowUnknownFields -> total CLI outage) and NOT a new auth_tier value (caller_rank defaults unknown tiers to 0 -> collapses public-read to anon and flips both guards to throw). Mirror the ?build/?chat/?bpml opt-in discipline in capabilities_controller.ex; thread the gating BEFORE the etag step (like maybe_gate_chat) so the key feeds etag_for/1. The membership predicate already exists (anon_perspective.ex:68 `"public-read" in perms`, documents_retriever.ex:369) -- echo it, invent no logic. If you add the key to the Go manifest model, land the struct field + the fetch.go param send in the SAME commit (a bp that asks and can't decode is a parse outage); bp need not send it, since only the templates consume the field -- if so, leave bp unchanged. Hand-edit docs/cli/manifest.schema.json (root additionalProperties:false) in the same PR. Add an Elixir contract test copying the ?build=1/?bpml=1 pattern (capabilities_manifest_test.exs:651/1316): ?perms=1 echoes the list; the default withholds the key. PART B -- tighten both guards. Change `tier === 'read'` to a `permissions.includes('public-read')` membership assertion in templates/astro-search-starter/astro.config.mjs AND templates/search-starter/next.config.mjs (both fetch ?perms=1). Add cases to the EXISTING templates/search-starter/token-guard.test.mjs (already CI-wired on both configs): a plain `read` token now reds the build; a [public-read,read] token passes (membership, not list-equality). Run `node --test token-guard.test.mjs` FIRST to confirm the harness is green before extending. CAUTION: tightening reds any live site whose baked token is a plain `read` mint -- enumerate live site tokens or note the deploy-breakage risk for the lead. This slice does NOT fix the scoped-search leak (dr-bl-scoped-search-private-leak) -- attestation half only.
